Auth here is per-route middleware, so "public" = any route not listed in a module's `configure()`. I read all four `configure()` blocks, every controller, and confirmed there's no global guard (`app.module.ts:21` — `providers: []`, no `APP_GUARD`). Global prefix is `/api` (`main.ts:8`).

## Public by design

| Endpoint | Handler | Guard source |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/articles` | `article.controller.ts:24` | not in `article.module.ts:23-31` |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug` | `article.controller.ts:38` | ″ |
| `GET /api/articles/:slug/comments` | `article.controller.ts:43` | ″ |
| `GET /api/profiles/:username` | `profile.controller.ts:18` | `profile.module.ts:22` guards only `:username/follow` |
| `GET /api/tags` | `tag.controller.ts:17` | `tag.module.ts:17-18` — `configure()` is **empty** |
| `POST /api/users` (register) | `user.controller.ts:32` | not in `user.module.ts:20` |
| `POST /api/users/login` | `user.controller.ts:43` | ″ |
| `GET /api` | `app.controller.ts:5` | `AppController` is in no module with middleware |
| `GET /docs` (Swagger UI) | `main.ts:18` | mounted outside the `/api` prefix, unguarded |

## Public by accident — this is the one to act on

**`DELETE /api/users/:slug`** — `user.controller.ts:37-40`. `UserModule.configure()` applies `AuthMiddleware` to exactly two routes, `GET /user` and `PUT /user` (`user.module.ts:20`); this delete is not among them. The handler passes `params.slug` straight to `UserService.delete()`, whose parameter is an **email** (`user.service.ts:83-84` — `userRepository.delete({ email: email })`).

Net effect: an unauthenticated `DELETE /api/users/someone@example.com` deletes that account. No token, no ownership comparison anywhere on the path.

## One nuance on the "public" reads

`GET /api/profiles/:username` is the only public route that still reads a token — `@User('id')` (`profile.controller.ts:19`) falls through to decoding the JWT itself when no middleware ran (`user.decorator.ts:12-17`). Two consequences:

- It's public but *identity-aware*: `following` is computed from the caller when a token is sent (`profile.service.ts:30`).
- That `jwt.verify` at `user.decorator.ts:15` is uncaught, so an expired or tampered token on this public route returns **500, not 401** — same defect as the middleware, already recorded in `LESSONS.md` (#79).

Separately, worth keeping straight: the eight guarded article routes (`article.module.ts:24-31`) require *a* token but compare the caller to nobody — `ArticleService.update()`/`delete()` have no owner check (`article.service.ts:197-198`), and the `@ApiResponse({status: 403})` annotations describe behaviour that isn't implemented. Ownership is already on the in-flight list in `CURRENT_FOCUS.md`.

**Not verified:** I read route registrations statically and did not run the app or issue requests, so this is what the code declares, not observed responses. There are no e2e tests in the repo to cross-check against (only `tag.controller.spec.ts`).
